question.question: Does Node preserve its guarantee that a configuration proposal is dropped unless there is no prior unapplied configuration, when its caller uses the documented early Advance optimization and defers ApplyConfChange in application order?
question.importance: Allowing a later configuration entry while the prior configuration is inactive bypasses the stated membership-serialization protection. The local admission defect may affect quorum-change safety, but the selected learner-only history measures no safety failure.

obligation.description: For callers complying with Node Ready/Advance ordering, a second proposed configuration change must not be appended as a configuration entry while an earlier committed configuration change has not yet been applied through ApplyConfChange (and has not been rejected by the application). The documented early Advance optimization does not itself apply the earlier configuration.

scope.description: Node-level configuration-proposal admission under documented early Advance, with persisted committed first change, delayed but ordered ApplyConfChange, and configuration validation enabled.

Prior configuration is intended to apply, not cancelled.

grounding.derivation: Node.ProposeConfChange states changes are dropped unless the leader is certain no prior unapplied configuration remains. Node.Advance explicitly permits overlap with application; doc.go permits any time after persistence, preserving application order. Configuration active membership changes at application. A caller-compliant early Advance therefore must not substitute for applying the configuration when admitting another change. This is local entry eligibility, not an inferred consensus safety theorem.
grounding.applicability: Node API, synchronous Ready/Advance, prior committed config not rejected by caller and deferred ApplyConfChange, ordered eventual application.
unresolved: An unstated configuration-specific exception to early Advance would change applicability; it is not present in the captured Node/package contract.
alternatives: Interpreting all Advance calls as completed application contradicts the Node-specific early-Advance permission, although that stronger description occurs on RawNode.

feedback.answered: The Node exploration completed all three histories. With Advance withheld, second index 4 is EntryNormal. Early Advance reports Applied=3 while userApplied=2 and no learners are active, then appends second index 4 as EntryConfChange before first ApplyConfChange. Apply-first control also appends EntryConfChange, with first application already complete. All histories subsequently complete ordered application. This is an exploratory admission difference; no global safety result follows.
